extracted.intended_audience: press officers and communications teams for clinical trial sponsors; clinical investigators and regulatory affairs staff preparing trial press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing press releases that report clinical trial registration, conduct, and results in compliance with ClinicalTrials.gov/FDA expectations and honest-science standards. Emphasizes mandatory disclosures, regulatory cautions for drugs/devices, and transparent reporting of results and harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable trials registered before initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain clinical trials must be registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before initiation as required by the Food and Drug Administration Amendments Act of 2007 (FDAAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of applicable trials prior to initiation is a statutory requirement; include registration details in communications and ensure trial was registered appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results submission within 1 year of primary completion
rubrics_metrics.description: ClinicalTrials.gov requires submission of results information within one year of the trial's primary completion date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should note results posting status and align public statements with whether results have been submitted/posted within the regulatory timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of both positive and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory reporting requires posting of both positive and negative trial results to reduce publication bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suppress negative outcomes in press communications; failure to report negative results contributes to publication bias and obscures true drug development outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of adverse events
rubrics_metrics.description: Adverse events must be reported to ClinicalTrials.gov and to the public where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should include a summary of adverse events and the overall safety profile rather than only highlighting efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of protocol details
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocol information (design, endpoints, etc.) is a required element of ClinicalTrials.gov reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include protocol-relevant details (e.g., primary endpoints, prespecification) or link to the registered protocol when issuing a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT number)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ClinicalTrials.gov identifier (NCT number) must be included in trial-related communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prominently include the NCT number and, where possible, link directly to the trial record so readers can verify registration and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration date
rubrics_metrics.description: State the date the trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the registration date helps readers assess whether registration was prospective and aligns with FDAAA expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results posting status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether results have been posted to ClinicalTrials.gov and the date/status of posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If results are not yet posted, note the expected timing and whether a results submission has been made to ClinicalTrials.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial sponsor named
rubrics_metrics.description: Name the trial sponsor in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the organization(s) responsible for the trial and provide contact information for follow-up or clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial phase specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the clinical trial phase (Phase I, II, III, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the developmental context clear — early-phase results should not be presented as definitive clinical benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the study design (e.g., randomized controlled trial, single-arm, observational).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity about design allows readers to judge the strength of evidence; avoid implying causal conclusions from non-randomized designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number of participants enrolled/analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include how many participants were randomized, analyzed for the primary endpoint, and any notable attrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary endpoint(s) reported
rubrics_metrics.description: State the pre-specified primary endpoint(s) of the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the exact primary outcome(s) as registered; do not substitute or emphasize secondary outcomes as the primary result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether endpoint(s) met
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report whether the primary endpoint(s) were achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish success/failure of pre-specified primary endpoints; avoid selective emphasis on favorable secondary or post-hoc outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish primary from secondary endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit which outcomes were primary (pre-specified) versus secondary or exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should be able to tell which findings were confirmatory versus hypothesis-generating; avoid conflating the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report effect sizes with confidence intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide effect size estimates accompanied by confidence intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative estimates with precision measures (e.g., 95% CI) give a clearer picture than p-values or qualitative statements alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note study limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limitations of the study design, sample, follow-up, or generalizability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about limitations reduces risk of overinterpretation; list important caveats rather than omitting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish hypothesis-generating from confirmatory findings
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether findings are exploratory/hypothesis-generating or confirmatory/definitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating exploratory subgroup or post-hoc findings as definitive evidence without proper replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgroup analyses explicitly noted
rubrics_metrics.description: If subgroup analyses are presented, state that they are subgroup/post-hoc analyses and interpret cautiously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify multiplicity and limitations of subgroup findings; avoid overinterpreting unplanned subgroup results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuations and attrition reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Report participant discontinuations and reasons where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discontinuations affect interpretation of results; provide numbers and causes (e.g., adverse events, withdrawal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding source disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose who funded the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify funders (industry, government, foundation) to allow readers to consider potential influences on study conduct or reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest (COIs) disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose financial or other conflicts of interest of investigators and sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List relevant COIs or provide a link to full COI disclosures; transparency supports credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA approval status clearly stated (drug/device releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the product is FDA-approved, and if so, for what indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make approval status unambiguous — do not imply approval for uses beyond the approved indication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved indication specified
rubrics_metrics.description: If a product is approved, specify the approved indication(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between the trial population/outcome and the approved indication to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-label use cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include cautions if discussing uses that are not FDA-approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn explicitly about off-label use and avoid language that encourages prescribing outside approved indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boxed warnings noted
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, note any boxed (black box) warnings associated with the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag severe or life-threatening risks required by FDA boxed warnings when communicating safety information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety profile summarized
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a balanced summary of the safety findings alongside efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize common and serious adverse events and contextualize safety relative to benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference required prescribing information
rubrics_metrics.description: When relevant, reference full prescribing information or label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to or cite prescribing information so clinicians/readers can access detailed safety and usage instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Investigational" status clearly stated (for investigational drugs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agent is investigational, the press release must clearly state it is not approved for marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly say 'investigational' and that the product is not approved and not for prescription outside trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not approved for marketing / not for prescription
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit that investigational products are not approved for marketing or prescription.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent misinterpretation that trial results equate to regulatory approval or allow routine clinical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial enrollment status
rubrics_metrics.description: State current trial enrollment status (e.g., completed, ongoing, actively recruiting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether results are interim, final, or from a completed cohort and whether further enrollment or follow-up is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare findings to prior literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextualize new results relative to existing studies and the broader evidence base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether results confirm, contradict, or extend previous findings; avoid presenting isolated results as definitive absent context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed publication if available
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide citation or link to the peer-reviewed article reporting the trial if one exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer linking to peer-reviewed publications for detailed methods and results; if not yet published, state that and provide ClinicalTrials.gov record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not oversell preliminary findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid language that overstates the clinical importance of preliminary, early-phase, or exploratory results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured language, emphasize preliminary nature where applicable, and avoid promotional phrasing that could mislead clinicians, patients, or investors.
